assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chemically induced proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system turns recognition chemistry into a general drug modality: heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues make 'undruggable' proteins addressable. This is exactly the kind of molecular design principle that changes what chemists and clinicians can do, with wide uptake in chemical biology and pharma.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept and its first proof of principle; Ciulli contributed the VHL ligand and structural rationale that made PROTACs drug-like. Handa/Ito (thalidomide-cereblon) and Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are strong claimants for the molecular-glue side, so a three-person split is contestable. My exact credit assessment relies on recalled history, not independent verification.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials and at least one has reached late-stage readouts, but approvals and long-term clinical validation are still limited. Recognition is plausible but could be slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and thalidomide-type molecular glues should be one prize or are two separable discoveries
Clinical outcomes still maturing
Priority disputes between early PROTAC work and cereblon biology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single nucleotides without double-strand cleavage by pairing deaminase chemistry with a programmable DNA-binding protein, and it was engineered through directed evolution. It created a new class of precision genome-editing tools and is already in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental development of both cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees and are credited, but a single-laureate award to Liu appears most defensible. Kondo and Nishida's parallel Target-AID work gives a legitimate second claim that complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many labs and in early clinical use, with a first patient treated; the field is moving fast. Timely, though the 2020 CRISPR prize makes the novelty framing a committee question.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 genome-editing prize and whether this counts as chemistry
Independent Target-AID priority
Long-term clinical safety and off-target editing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the delivery chemistry that made siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines work in humans. The impact on medicine is immense and demonstrated at global scale, and the design logic (pH-dependent charge for encapsulation and endosomal release) is a clear molecular principle.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues at UBC developed the lipid nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid approach; Langer's group contributed broad lipid and polymer delivery systems and combinatorial lipid libraries, with Anderson an important collaborator. Credit is spread across many groups and companies, so any three-person selection is a judgment call. Names here are recalled, not verified.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: licensed siRNA drug (patisiran) and billions of mRNA vaccine doses. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, though the 2023 Medicine prize touched adjacent work on nucleoside modification.
uncertainties: Dispersed credit across academic and industrial inventors
Patent-driven priority disputes
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or pharmaceutical technology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat showed that a mutant cysteine in KRAS G12C can be covalently targeted through a switch-II pocket, and earlier developed analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics. The work cracked a target long thought undruggable and led directly to approved drugs, a rare clean path from molecular design to patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: A single-author candidate, which is attractive for allocation. Shokat's lab made the decisive KRAS G12C finding; drug development at Amgen, Mirati and others built on it, and covalent-inhibitor precedents from other fields exist, so I would accept a narrowly framed credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved KRAS G12C inhibitors (sotorasib, adagrasib) provide strong confirmation, and subsequent generations of RAS inhibitors validate the principle. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should be framed around KRAS or chemical genetics more broadly
Contributions of company scientists to the drugs
Durability of clinical responses given resistance

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed noncanonical amino acids at defined positions through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. It gives chemists site-specific control over protein chemistry in living systems, with wide uses in biophysics, biotherapeutics and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first orthogonal pair and the general approach; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms, quadruplet codons and synthetic genomes; Wang contributed early expansion work in the Schultz lab and later neuroscience applications. Yokoyama and Mehl also have strong claims, so the three-person pick leaves out meaningful contributors.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and adopted widely for over two decades; several protein therapeutics using it are in development. Mature, with credit assessment well settled in the field.
uncertainties: Attribution among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Yokoyama and Mehl
Limited clinical translation so far
Competing proximity to the 2018 directed-evolution prize themes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses covalent probes to read the functional state of enzymes in complex proteomes, linking reactivity chemistry to biology and drug discovery. It introduced chemoproteomic target and ligand discovery, including the current surge in covalent fragment screening.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt and Bogyo (with Overkleeft and the earlier Cravatt/Bogyo-era probe developers) hold the principal claims; Weerapana is a key contributor on cysteine reactivity. Cravatt is the most consistent originator of the field's broad framework. Credit lines to Overkleeft and others are unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted, with probe-derived and covalent ligands entering the clinic. The most recent chemoproteomic directions are still maturing.
uncertainties: Dividing credit between Cravatt, Bogyo and Overkleeft
Clinical impact is indirect
Overlap with other proteomics and covalent-drug discovery work

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics, including shotgun sequencing, quantitative labeling and label-free approaches, turned protein analysis into a systems-scale measurement. It is a foundation of modern biomedicine, from biomarker discovery to interaction mapping, and is a bioanalytical advance I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are widely viewed as leaders of the methodology (SILAC and high-resolution workflows, targeted/SRM and SWATH, and shotgun/MudPIT respectively). Hunt, Gygi and Heck also made decisive contributions, so the field's credit is crowded and any three-person limit is uncomfortable.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and broadly confirmed; the technique is routine. The 2002 prize for ionization methods covers an adjacent step, but proteomics itself has had decades of validation.
uncertainties: Crowded attribution with at least six strong contributors
Overlap with the Orbitrap and native MS candidates
Whether the 2002 prize reduces appetite for another mass spectrometry award

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids made nanoparticle surface chemistry programmable and turned it into colorimetric biosensing and intracellular gene regulation. This is closely related to my own work on gold-nanoparticle plasmonic sensors, which colors my enthusiasm and my caution about conflict of interest in judging it.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group established the DNA-gold nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acid architecture, with Storhoff and Mucic as key coauthors; Alivisatos independently reported DNA-nanocrystal organization at the same time. Mirkin and Alivisatos are the natural pair, and Alivisatos has other claims through nanocrystal science.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated, with commercialized diagnostics and clinical-stage therapeutics, but the clinical impact is narrower than for other candidates and still developing.
uncertainties: Alivisatos's broader nanocrystal contributions may belong to a different prize case
Limited clinical translation to date
Possible bias from my close research proximity
